title: The Broken Landfall
premise: Paloma Oyelaran, a salvage diver scraping a living from the drowned wrecks of the Vessarine coast, recovers a sealed chest stamped with the crest of Kethria, a nation erased from every map forty years ago. The chest holds proof that Kethria's fall was engineered by the very admiralty now paying to keep its waters silent, and inside is an inheritance: coordinates, a name, and a claim that legally belongs to whoever carries it home. Hunted by naval contractors and betrayed by the expedition's own patron, Paloma must lead her ragged crew upriver through flood season to reach a neutral archive before the navy can bury the evidence — and them. The book ends with Paloma surrendering the inheritance to the archive rather than claiming it, choosing memory over power, and watching the truth surface like a wreck she finally lets go of.
about_author: E. M. Vane is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent six years charting river deltas before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose livelihoods depend on what the water gives back.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. On a routine salvage dive over a wreck the navy forbids discussion of, Paloma finds a lead-lined chest stamped with Kethria's seal. Her crewmate Doss wants to sell it; she wants to open it. The beat is wary curiosity — the first crack in a life built on not asking questions.

chapters.title: The Dead Nation's Seal
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The chest resists opening until Paloma notices the lock reads a date, not a key. Inside: documents, a brass astrolabe, and a deed of inheritance naming a bearer. Emotional beat: dread dressed as excitement, as she realizes the navy's silence has a price tag.

chapters.title: A Patron with Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Expedition financier Corvel Asque offers to fund a full recovery dive — too generously, too fast. Paloma hides the deed but accepts the money, telling herself she's using him. Beat: self-deception; power begins its quiet offer.

chapters.title: Crew of the Second Chance
chapters.summary: POV Doss. Doss recruits the expedition crew: engineer Sefa, ex-naval cartographer Ilya, and teenager Runi who knows the river shallows. Each has a reason to need money and none asks why the navy cares. Beat: found-family warmth established so it can be tested later.

chapters.title: Flood Season Rules
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The Second Chance departs upriver ahead of the floods, racing a window that closes in nineteen days. First night, a navy patrol boat shadows them without hailing. Beat: the wilderness as antagonist — indifferent, precise, unforgiving.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. Ilya dives the forbidden wreck and recognizes naval scuttle charges on a civilian hull. He says nothing to Paloma yet, carrying the knowledge like ballast. Beat: complicity — how corruption recruits ordinary people one secret at a time.

chapters.title: Asque's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Runi. Snooping for stowaway space, Runi finds Asque's ledger: payments from the Admiralty Office, dated before the chest was ever found. She tells only Doss, who pockets the page. Beat: betrayal seeded in desperation.

chapters.title: Rapids at Kessel Bend
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A run through flood-swollen rapids nearly kills Runi; Paloma goes in after her and loses the spare air tanks. The crew bonds harder — but Asque uses the loss to argue for turning back, his real goal being the chest alone. Beat: loyalty forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Kethria's Last Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. They reach a drowned town, intact below the waterline. Murals show Kethria's fall: not war, but a manufactured famine signed off by admirals whose names still head the navy. Beat: grief for the dead nation; the theme of memory made physical.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. Deciphering the deed, Ilya learns the bearer can claim reparations funds frozen for forty years — enough to buy fleets. Asque reveals he knows, and offers Paloma a cut to hand it over. Beat: temptation sharpened into a blade.

chapters.title: Doss Sells the Page
chapters.summary: POV Doss. Doss sells Asque's ledger page to a naval contractor skiff in exchange for passage out. Watching the boat leave, he feels nothing he expected. Beat: guilt arriving late, the way it always does.

chapters.title: Contractors at the Weir
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Navy contractors board at the old fishing weir. Ilya's forged charts buy an hour; Sefa's engine work buys their escape through a flooded channel no chart admits exists. Beat: competence as resistance; the crew chooses each other over safety.

chapters.title: What Ilya Buried
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. Cornered, Ilya confesses he helped survey the original cover-up as a young cartographer and stayed silent for thirty years. Paloma must decide whether his penance buys trust. Beat: memory as burden; forgiveness withheld, then granted.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Asque takes the chest at gunpoint during a supply stop, leaving the crew stranded with a holed hull. Paloma realizes the deed matters more than the chest — the inheritance lives in the bearer, not the box. Beat: despair transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: River Country Allies
chapters.summary: POV Runi. Runi's kin along the banks shelter the crew, repair the hull, and pass word ahead: the archive at Verren Reach will hear a bearer's claim if she arrives before the flood crests. Beat: community as counterweight to institutional power.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Divide
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A two-day running chase through the canyon divide, Asque's hired gunboats behind, the rising river ahead. Sefa rigs a decoy light; Doss, unasked, stays behind to spring it. Beat: sacrifice offered without guarantee of redemption.

chapters.title: Verren Reach
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. They reach the neutral archive as the flood swallows the lower town. The archivists are cautious, bureaucratic, unmoved by heroics — they want procedure, not passion. Beat: frustration; the truth needs more than courage to survive.

chapters.title: The Claim Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma presents the deed and Ilya's testimony. Asque arrives with Admiralty lawyers and the recovered chest, claiming theft. The hearing pivots on one question: who does an inheritance belong to when its owners were murdered? Beat: climax of argument, not violence.

chapters.title: Power Refused
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Offered the fortune outright if she withdraws the criminal allegations, Paloma instead surrenders the entire inheritance to the archive as public record — reparations for Kethria's survivors' descendants, none of it hers. Beat: the thematic summit; power declined is power defeated.

chapters.title: Asque's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Ilya. With the record public, the Admiralty cuts Asque loose to save itself; contractors detain him at the dock. Ilya testifies fully, ending his thirty-year silence. Beat: justice as consequence, cold and administrative rather than triumphant.

chapters.title: High Water, Clear Sky
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Flood peak passes. The crew buries Doss's decoy lantern where he last stood, and Runi carves his name into the Second Chance's rail. Beat: mourning braided with gratitude; the family that survived its own fractures.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Months later, Paloma dives again — ordinary wrecks, honest pay. News arrives that Kethria's name is returning to maps. She surfaces into sunlight, lets the river take the last of the old secrets, and signs the charter for a new expedition. Beat: resolution; memory honored, the future open.
